summary: Meerut Police arrested two brothers, Hafiz Aman and Faizan, for running a multi-state cyber fraud racket. Posing as carpet sellers on Facebook, they collected advance payments from traders across nine states and disappeared. An associate, Akram, is absconding. They cheated victims of nearly Rs 10 lakh.

The Karnataka State Cyber Command busted four fake call centres in Bengaluru that impersonated US-based accounting firm Quick Book. They arrested two accused, Prashanth from Delhi and Akash from Uttar Pradesh, who used shell companies like Circle Square LLC to scam US citizens with fake tax and licensing services.

Lakhimpur Kheri district police arrested 12 alleged members of an organized cyber fraud gang operating online scams. The gang used fake SIM cards, mobile phones, and digital payment channels. Police seized mobile phones, SIM cards, and cash, and are tracing bank accounts and potential interstate links.

Rawatpur police in Kanpur arrested two cyber fraudsters, Sumeet Kashyap and Naveen Srivastava, for supplying mule accounts to a syndicate led by absconding Delhi-based mastermind Tomar. The gang is linked to a Rs 14 crore transaction trail, 13 complaints across 13 states, and cheating an engineer of Rs 97 lakh.

Kanpur Police arrested eight members of a gang that extorted close to Rs 2 crore. Posing as CBI or crime branch officers, they blackmailed victims (mostly women) by falsely accusing them of watching child pornography. The gang played siren sounds on video calls and sent torture videos to intimidate victims.

UP Police busted an inter-state cyber fraud racket in Revna, Kanpur, and arrested 19 youths. The gang duped hundreds by posing as government welfare scheme facilitators, using fake documents and mule bank accounts to siphon off funds. Mobile phones, forged documents, and mule account details were recovered.

Uttar Pradesh Police arrested 34 suspects and tracked 45 others during extensive raids targeting rural cybercrime networks in Janghawali and Bishambhara villages, Mathura. The syndicate, linked to 18 cases, used fake Aadhaar cards and multiple mobile phones. Eight of the arrested suspects were repeat offenders.

UP Police busted an inter-state cyber fraud syndicate in Bareilly with suspected connections to Nepal and Chinese handlers. They arrested five accused (Shakib Ali, Rajkumar, Ashish Singh, Babloo, Sachendra Kumar) and are searching for absconding kingpin Sumit Kumar. The gang used 22 bank accounts linked to 524 complaints.

A Noida family, including an MBBS student and two retired officials, was subjected to a five-day 'digital arrest' by scammers posing as CBI officers over WhatsApp video calls. The scammers threatened them with fake terror-linked allegations, extorted nearly Rs 3 lakh, and kept them under continuous video surveillance before neighbours rescued them.

Kanpur Police busted a 'mini Jamtara' cyber fraud network in the Reuna area of Ghatampur, arresting 20 fraudsters. Posing as police officers or offering fake housing schemes, the gang operated from huts in fields. Police used drones and seized laptops, phones, active SIMs, and mule accounts. Fifteen suspects fled.

UP Police conducted pre-dawn raids deploying over 200 personnel in Shergarh, Mathura, detaining over 50 suspected cyber fraudsters. The syndicate was involved in identity theft, fake job offers, bogus investment schemes, and digital arrest scams. Police seized mobile phones, SIM cards, and transaction logs, revealing interstate links.

Kanpur police busted an organized cyber fraud racket with international links, arresting eight suspects involved in online gaming-based scams on apps like Lotus365 and Reddy Book. The network operated from Dubai, using fake bank accounts to route over Rs 50 lakh.

Mathura police arrested 34 suspects and tracked 45 others during pre-dawn raids in Vishambhara and Jhanjhawali villages near Shergarh (called 'Mini Jamtara'). The gang was involved in phishing, online scams, and digital extortion targeting victims across India and abroad.

Gorakhpur Cyber Cell arrested seven members of a cyber fraud syndicate. The gang lured poor villagers into opening bank accounts under the pretext of government schemes like Vishwakarma Shram Samman Yojana, using the accounts as mule accounts to channel cyber fraud proceeds.

Kanpur police busted an inter-state cyber fraud gang, arresting 19 youths. Operating from a fake call center, the suspects lured victims under the pretext of providing welfare scheme benefits, subsequently using fake documents and mule accounts to launder the proceeds.

Ahmedabad police booked a Gujarat resident from Gomtipur whose bank account was utilized as a mule account for cyber fraud across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh. Transactions totaling lakhs of rupees were routed through the account.

Balrampur Police busted an interstate cyber fraud network and arrested five suspects. The gang conducted illegal financial transactions worth over Rs 58 crore using forged documents to open multiple bank accounts. Mobile phones, SIM cards, ATM cards, and fake IDs were seized.

Two youths from Barabanki, UP, were arrested by Haryana police for defrauding a Sonipat resident, Omprakash, of Rs 4.49 lakh. Posing as a relative over a WhatsApp call, the fraudsters claimed a medical emergency and shared a fake bank statement showing a false credit.

Mirzapur police busted an interstate cyber fraud racket, arresting eight suspects. The gang utilized 11,605 mobile phones and forged documents to steal citizen identities and open fake bank accounts for laundering. Police seized mobile phones, laptops, and cash.
An 85-year-old man in Lucknow became the victim of a cyber fraud, losing Rs 84.5 lakh. The case highlights the vulnerability of senior citizens to digital financial crimes in the region.

Prayagraj police busted a fake marksheet syndicate operating in Uttar Pradesh and arrested three suspects. The gang issued forged educational documents of the State Open School to candidates for money.

UP STF busted a racket rigging SSC online recruitment exams using proxy servers and dummy candidates at Balaji Digital Zone in Greater Noida. They arrested seven suspects and seized Rs 50 lakh in cash. The gang charged candidates Rs 4 lakh each. Four accomplices are absconding.

Mathura police arrested 34 suspects and tracked 45 others during pre-dawn raids in Vishambhara and Jhanjhawali villages near Shergarh (called 'Mini Jamtara'). The gang was involved in phishing, online scams, and digital extortion targeting victims across India and abroad.

Uttar Pradesh police arrested a former branch manager of a cooperative bank Maharajganj branch in Gonda in connection with a Rs 21-crore loan scam. In a related case, police in Kakori arrested a Bank of Baroda correspondent for siphoning off customer deposits, affecting over 50 customers.

Vikas Rana, a resident of Silver Nagar, Baghpat, UP, who was lured to Cambodia under a fake job offer and forced into cyber slavery by a cyber-fraud syndicate, was rescued and repatriated to India through Baghpat police coordination with the I4C and the Indian Embassy.

Basti district police arrested six members of a Mewat-based cyber crime network operating a mule account racket. The gang lured rural villagers into opening bank accounts and seized their ATM cards and documents. A total of 38 bank accounts linked to over 74 fraud cases totaling over Rs 4.49 crore were uncovered.

Delhi Police arrested B.A. student and Instagram influencer Hukum Singh Rawat alias Anuj from Lucknow for aiding an inter-state online fraud syndicate in a Rs 1.8 lakh tractor sale scam. Rawat received commission for providing bank accounts to launder funds under the direction of co-accused Rahul.

Bundi cybercrime police arrested Jitendra Vaishnav for his involvement in an inter-state cyber fraud syndicate. The gang defrauded people across 15 states under the pretext of online gaming and investments. Transactions worth Rs 4.85 crore were conducted through accounts opened by local youths.

Lucknow police tracked a massive mule account network used to launder cyber fraud proceeds into USDT crypto via P2P networks for handlers in Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos, and Thailand. Police detained around 60 young men who rented their accounts for commissions. One holder, Ajay, turned approver.

Azamgarh Cyber Crime Police busted an international cyber fraud syndicate linked to Rs 110 crore in frauds. The gang hacked victims' phones using malicious APK files (PM Kisan/E-Challan) via Instagram and Telegram. Police arrested 15 suspects, including Parvez Ansari and Mohammad Kaleem, while prime accused Imran Ali is at large.

Azamgarh Cyber Crime Police busted an international cyber fraud syndicate linked to Rs 110 crore in frauds. The gang hacked victims' phones using malicious APK files (PM Kisan/E-Challan) via Instagram and Telegram. Police arrested 15 suspects, including Parvez Ansari and Mohammad Kaleem, while prime accused Imran Ali is at large.

UP STF arrested three members of an organized cyber gang in Kolkata for creating fake Instagram pages of reputed chikankari companies. They lured customers with fake invoices edited via picsart and collected payments through UPI IDs provided by associate Rohit Manna.

A mechanical engineer, Krishna Kumar, was arrested in Noida for running a Rs 6.03 crore online stock trading scam. Kumar targeted victims via social media, persuading them to join a Telegram channel named 'Plus500 Global CS' where fake profit screenshots were displayed. Rs 57 lakh was traced to his front company.

A Noida-based private firm employee, Neha, was extorted of Rs 13.42 lakh by cyber fraudsters in Agra. Posing as couriers and law enforcement officials, they put her under 'digital arrest' for four days after claiming a drug-laced parcel was intercepted in Bangkok.

UP Police's cyber crime wing unearthed pan-India frauds totaling Rs 4,200 crore linked to operators based in China. The scams involved crypto currency trading, instant loan apps, and fake job advertisements using fake websites and bulk SMSes.

A Class 8 student in Bareilly prevented a cyber fraud by cutting off a video call after fraudsters held his parents, Sanjay Saxena and his wife, under a fake 'digital arrest' for nearly 10 hours. The scammers had accused them of terror links using a fake arrest warrant.

Delhi Police arrested six mule account operators in Lucknow for running a 'digital arrest' fraud. Posing as law-enforcement personnel over video calls, they duped a 71-year-old woman of Rs 49 lakh, holding her under digital confinement for nearly 24 hours. Stolen funds were moved and immediately withdrawn from ATMs.

An elderly couple in Ghaziabad was duped of Rs 2.86 crore after being placed under 'digital arrest' and surveillance for 12 days. Scammers posing as CBI officers, a prosecutor, and Maharashtra Police accused them of money laundering, forcing them to liquidate their fixed deposits and mutual funds.

Agra police arrested three cybercriminals, exposing an international digital arrest syndicate run by Chinese operators in Cambodia, Vietnam, and Laos. The syndicate hires Indian agents to recruit unemployed youths, send them abroad, confiscate their passports, and force them to execute extortion calls posing as CBI, ED, or police officers.

A 30-year-old Bijnor housewife, Monica Singh, committed suicide by hanging after being blackmailed and held under 'digital arrest' by cyber fraudsters. Fraudsters posing as Crime Branch officers threatened her over WhatsApp video calls. The threats continued even after her death, targetting her family.

Shivamogga police arrested two men from Uttar Pradesh (Mohammed Ahmed and Abhishek Kumar Shet) for extorting Rs 41 lakh from 72-year-old senior citizen L.S. Anand. Scammers posing as Telecom Department and Mumbai Police officers put him under a video call 'digital arrest' over money laundering allegations.

Two Canadian NRI sisters, Suman Kakkar and Vinay Thapliyal, were duped of nearly Rs 1.9 crore in Lucknow after being 'digitally arrested' by scammers posing as Mumbai Crime Branch officers. They threatened them with money laundering and terror charges. Cyber cell frozen Rs 25 lakh.

Ajmer police arrested Omkar Singh in Didwana-Kuchaman for providing his bank account to fraudsters who placed Kanpur resident Anurag Kumar under 'digital arrest'. Scammers posing as BHEL representatives claimed a drug-laced parcel in Anurag's name was intercepted, extorting Rs 5.18 lakh.

UP STF arrested two Nepalese nationals, Saroj Khanal and Shivram Rimal, in Lucknow for conducting digital fraud, including 'digital arrest' scams. Posing as Indian nationals using forged Aadhaar cards, they coordinated with a Chinese operative named Ben based in Nepal to manage mule accounts.

Dr. Ruchika Tandon, an associate professor at SGPGIMS Lucknow, was duped of Rs 2.81 crore after being placed under 'digital arrest'. Scammers posing as TRAI officials and police officer Rahul G accused her of sending harassment messages, forcing her to transfer funds to seven accounts.

Odisha Crime Branch arrested a mother-son duo, Neelam and Vansh Aggarwal, in Ghaziabad for extorting Rs 1.37 crore from a retired Bhubaneswar engineer. Posing as couriers and Mumbai police, they put him under 'digital arrest' for a week over fake money laundering charges.

Noida Cyber Police arrested Mukesh Saxena and Anees Ahmed of Moradabad for defrauding a Noida resident of Rs 2.39 crore through a 'digital arrest' scam. Posing as law enforcement officers, they threatened the victim with fake human trafficking and money laundering charges, forcing him to transfer funds.

An investigation by The Eastern Herald uncovered a subscription scam targeting India's online creator community via platforms like XHOPP, GuardLynk, and HAXCEL. Scammers sold fake enterprise invitations and subscriptions (e.g. for Adobe), then revoked access and threatened victims.

Model and former Femina Miss India West Bengal 2017 Shivankita Dixit was duped of Rs 99,000 in Agra after being placed under 'digital arrest' for two hours. A scammer named Rahul posed as a courier agent and CBI officer, threatening her with drug trafficking charges.

Santosh Kumar Sharma, a government employee in Aligarh, lost Rs 10.85 lakh from his Bank of Baroda account through 12 unauthorized UPI transactions. Sharma, who never activated UPI on his account, reported the fraud via the 1930 helpline, leading to account freezing.

Hardoi police arrested 10 educated suspects, including B.Tech students Harshit, Anshuman, and Arjun from a Lucknow college, for running a cyber fraud network. The gang cheated people across the country through fake gaming apps and online platforms using rented bank accounts.

Agra cyber cell exposed a high-tech cybercrime network that defrauded victims across India of over Rs 30 crore. Over 15 months, the syndicate used more than 7,000 fake mobile numbers and UPI IDs registered under forged documents of unsuspecting laborers and street vendors.

Gulriha police in Gorakhpur registered an FIR against 21 accused for defrauding real estate businessman Vishwajeet Srivastava of Rs 24 crore. The suspects, including Sonu Jaiswal and Shivam Jaiswal, edited transaction visuals on laptops to create fake UPI payment screenshots.

UP STF arrested Om Kumar of Patna in Lucknow's Sushant Golf City for defrauding exam candidates. Kumar falsely claimed on social media and Telegram that he could leak the CNET 2026 paper, collecting money from candidates through UPI.

A 20-year-old Noida boy named Deepak received a mistaken credit of Rs 1.13 lakh crore in his deceased mother's Kotak Mahindra Bank account. The bank froze the account and the Income Tax Department began an investigation to determine if it was a technical error or money laundering.

Agra police arrested 62-year-old Ramveer Singh in Greater Noida, solving a 17-year-old insurance fraud case. Singh and accomplice Anil Singh had killed a beggar, dressed him in Anil's clothes, and burned him in a staged car crash to claim Anil's Rs 60 lakh life insurance policy.

UP STF arrested Hawaldar Naresh Kumar in Meerut for running an Agniveer recruitment fraud. Kumar and his brother Saurabh promised candidates they would pass the medical exam at Military Hospital Meerut for Rs 5 lakh. Kumar had been running the scam for four years, making Rs 35 lakh.

Azamgarh police busted an interstate cybercrime syndicate that defrauded investors of nearly Rs 1 crore using a fake trading app 'Next Trade' promoted on Facebook. They arrested bank employee Ankesh Dhakad and Indrajeet Dey. The gang used mule accounts aided by bank insiders.

Shahjahanpur authorities ordered the attachment of assets worth Rs 4.49 crore belonging to dismissed social welfare officer Rajesh Kumar, the alleged kingpin of a large-scale old-age pension scam. The gang systematically siphoned public pension funds by altering bank account details in official systems.

Noida Police arrested six people, including graduate Tanishka, for operating a fake OTT subscription scam that duped 37,000 NRIs in the US and Germany. Using pirated apps offering 13 streaming platforms at half price, they sourced customer data from the dark web and contacted victims via virtual phone software.

Lucknow police arrested Dhairya Verma and Maruf Asif Kasmani for using a Telegram bot to access online shoppers' data on the dark web. They defrauded Amazon Pay and Amazon Pay Later customers of crores by making unauthorized online purchases of protein powders, mobile phones, and other items.

The Uttar Pradesh government unearthed a Rs 500 crore fertiliser scam involving fictitious sales of approximately 100,000 quintals of fertiliser to farmers using fake identities. The stock was black-marketed, including over 23,000 quintals in Gorakhpur district.

A farmer in Kolhapur lost Rs 5 lakh after his 11-year-old son downloaded a game on his smartphone and clicked a link to buy virtual firearms. Scammers hacked the phone and siphoned the money from a UPI-linked account. The incident was investigated by the Kolhapur Cyber police.

Kaushambi police in Ghaziabad busted a dating app scam, arresting eight suspects (including five women, Khalid alias Imran, Nadeem, and Sumit) at Tiger Café near Kaushambi Metro. The gang lured men via dating apps, charged exorbitant bills, held them hostage, and extorted money.

UP Police busted a Rs 500-crore cyber fraud operated by teenage suspects from a luxury penthouse in Lucknow. Posing as gaming app 'Anna Reddy', they duped over 2.5 lakh victims across South India. Operations were headed by Vishal Yadav from Dubai, with links to Sri Lanka.

Kerala Police arrested three UP natives (Rishikesh Tiwari, Prasanth Gheval, and Prakash Jai) in Noida for loan app fraud linked to the suicide of BDS student Nithin Raj R L. The accused ran 'Instant Funds' and 'Insta Pay', charging 36% interest and harassing the victim.

Mumbai Police arrested five youths from Uttar Pradesh for defrauding a retired banker, Iyer, of Rs 7 lakh in a stock trading scam. Posing as Wall Street expert Jaykumar Verma, the scammers lured the victim on WhatsApp into joining a trading group and investing via a fake app 'm.Amansa.net'.

Kerala Cyber Police arrested Athul Kumar Singh and Maneesh Yadav in Varanasi for running a nationwide Parivahan app fraud. Aided by a 16-year-old relative who developed the fake app, they sent malicious APK files via WhatsApp under the guise of vehicle fines, siphoning money from victims.

Meerut cyber police arrested four suspects (Sanjay Sarkar, Mohit Sarkar, Subramanyam Yamalvalasa, and Harsh Sarkar) for running a fake online medicine delivery scam. The accused, former employees of a Noida medicine firm, stole database logs and duped at least 37 victims of Rs 20 lakh.

UP STF arrested a youth from Agra for defrauding candidates by falsely claiming to leak the Sub-Inspector recruitment exam paper. The suspect operated a Telegram channel to lure candidates with fake question PDFs, collecting money from them.

An Indore play school owner lost Rs 97,500 in Madhya Pradesh's first AI voice-cloning scam. Scammers used voice modulation technology to clone her cousin's voice (who works with UP Police) and fabricated a medical emergency, tricking her into transferring her savings.

UPSC aspirant Anurag Mishra discovered a negative lien of Rs 25.59 crore in his ICICI bank account. Scammers had misused his PAN details to open a current account in Varanasi, set up a fake GST firm, and availed loans worth crores in his name.

Noida Cyber Police arrested Mohammed Riyaz and Liaq Ahmed, members of a Jamtara-based gang, for a Rs 5.97 lakh online fraud. Posing as bank help desk agents through fake Google search ads, they took remote access of a Ghaziabad woman's phone to steal OTPs and drain her account.
